title: Fastify Adapter (platform-fastify): Routing Performance vs Express

progressiveExplaining.eli5: By default, NestJS uses Express as its delivery engine (reliable, but built on older JavaScript). Fastify is a modern rocket engine for web servers: it uses hyper-optimized routing and lightning-fast JSON serialization, doubling the number of requests your server can handle per second with a two-line configuration change.
progressiveExplaining.junior: NestJS is platform-agnostic: it uses Express by default (`@nestjs/platform-express`), but you can switch to Fastify by installing `@nestjs/platform-fastify` and initializing `NestFactory.create(AppModule, new FastifyAdapter())`. Fastify provides up to **2x higher throughput (RPS)** and lower latency than Express due to its radix-tree router and fast JSON serializer (`fast-json-stringify`).
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `FastifyAdapter` replaces Express's linear array middleware matching with a **Radix Tree (Find-My-Way)** router, achieving `O(k)` URL route lookup (where `k` is URL length) instead of `O(N)` route matching. It avoids Express's synchronous `res.send()` buffer overhead by using schema-based serialization. Trade-offs: Express-specific middleware (e.g. `multer`, `passport` without fastify session wrappers) must be replaced with Fastify plugins (`@fastify/multipart`).
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: `FastifyAdapter` implements `AbstractHttpAdapter`. When `app.listen()` executes, NestJS compiles route metadata into Fastify route definitions (`fastify.route()`). Fastify pre-compiles route parameter regexes into radix tree nodes. When returning JSON, Fastify uses pre-compiled schema serializers to write string fragments directly into the HTTP response stream.

interviewGotchas.question: What is the common host binding mistake when deploying a NestJS Fastify app inside a Docker container?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: This is the classic production deployment gotcha with Fastify.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Express binds to `0.0.0.0` (all network interfaces) by default. Fastify binds to `127.0.0.1` (localhost only) by default. If you deploy a Fastify app inside a Docker container and call `await app.listen(3000)`, the container port will **not be reachable from outside the container**. You **must pass `'0.0.0.0'` explicitly**: `await app.listen(3000, '0.0.0.0')`.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Forgetting `'0.0.0.0'` in `app.listen(3000)` causes container health checks and ingress routing to fail with connection refused.

interviewGotchas.question: Can you use standard Express middleware (like `app.use(morgan())`) with Fastify in NestJS?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of middleware compatibility layers.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: No. Standard Express middleware relies on the `(req, res, next)` signature and Express-specific methods (like `res.send()`). With `FastifyAdapter`, you must use native Fastify plugins (e.g. `@fastify/helmet`, `@fastify/cors`) or register them using `app.register()`.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Attempting to use `@Res() res: express.Response` in a Fastify controller will result in undefined method crashes (`res.status is not a function`).
